prompt:
I need the front end for Studiofold. A shared project workspace that a seven-person brand identity studio pays for, holding every client job's phases, presentations, source files and feedback rounds in one place.

Who's using it: Ines Varga, a mid-level designer at Northpaw Studio in Lisbon. She has just come back from three weeks of leave and wasn't involved in the second half of the Halden Coffee rebrand. She knows design tools well but doesn't yet know how her colleagues organised this particular project while she was away.

What they're doing right now: Halden's marketing lead just phoned and said she wants to go back to 'the wordmark with the open counter from the second presentation, but in the warmer palette from the last one'. Ines has to work out which presentation that was, find the slide and the exact source file behind that wordmark, then find where the warmer palette was defined. From there she needs to get to the type exploration it came from, and to the client's written feedback on round two, to make sure that direction wasn't rejected for a reason. She keeps losing track of which round and which folder she's in, and needs to get back to the project's top level quickly to start a new round 4.

What's in the system at this point: 23 active client projects and 61 archived. The Halden Coffee project has four phases (Discovery, Concepts, Refinement, Rollout). It holds three client presentations (R1 12 Sep, R2 3 Oct, R3 31 Oct 2026), each with 18–34 slides. There are 147 source files (wordmark explorations, palettes, packaging mockups, a 9-file type exploration set) tagged by round and author, 4 client feedback documents, and 38 internal comments. Studio members: Rui (creative director), Ines, Tomás, Ama, Kit, Lena, and Joon (producer). Each file has a version count, last editor and date, and which presentations it appears in. The R2 wordmark is 'Halden_WM_open-c_v7' and the warm palette is 'Palette_R3_ember'.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
